config.title: Star Rating Component

intro.title: Star Rating Component
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive Star Rating component that allows users to select and display a rating from one to five stars. You will learn how to manage component state to track the current rating and the user's hover selection. The core programming concepts involve using React's useState hook for state management and handling user events like clicks and mouse interactions. You'll implement this by creating a reusable component that renders star icons and updates visually based on user input, using JSX for structure and JavaScript for logic.
intro.usecase: Star rating components are essential interactive UI elements found across modern web applications. You'll implement them in e-commerce product pages for customer reviews, in streaming platforms for content ratings, and in feedback forms for user satisfaction surveys. As a React developer, you'll build these reusable components to collect user input and display aggregated ratings consistently. Mastering this pattern prepares you for real-world scenarios like creating review systems for marketplaces or rating interfaces for service platforms.

objectives: Implement a React component that renders a star rating interface
Initialize and manage component state to track the current rating
Configure click handlers to update the rating based on user interaction
Render dynamic star icons that visually reflect the selected rating
Bind mouse events to provide interactive hover feedback
Control the component's behavior through props for customization
Integrate the star rating component into a larger application context

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for React and useState are added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the StarRating component function
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named StarRating that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called StarRating that returns null. You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the StarRating component function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A StarRating component function is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The StarRating function is defined and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the StarRating component function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the function is named StarRating and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The StarRating component function isn't defined correctly. Check the function name and return value.

steps.title: Initialize rating state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the StarRating component function, use useState to declare a state variable named 'rating' and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Call useState(0) and destructure the returned array into two variables: the state variable and its setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a 'rating' state variable that starts at 0, ready to track the user's selected star rating.
successCriteria: The component function contains a useState call that declares a 'rating' variable initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with an initial value of 0 and destructuring it into a variable named 'rating'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rating state isn't properly initialized. Remember to call useState(0) inside the component and destructure the result into [rating, setRating].

steps.title: Initialize hover state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your StarRating component, use useState to create a state variable named 'hover' and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Add another useState call similar to how you initialized the rating state. The syntax is: const [hover, setHover] = useState(0);
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a numeric state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: 'rating' and 'hover', both initialized to 0.
successCriteria: A 'hover' state variable is declared using useState and initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState to create a variable named 'hover' initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use useState to create a state variable named 'hover' with an initial value of 0.

steps.title: Define handleRatingClick function
steps.instruction: Inside your StarRating component, define a function named handleRatingClick that takes a starNumber parameter and updates the rating state with that value.
steps.hint: Create a function that uses setRating to update the state. The function should be defined inside the component body.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleRatingClick function is defined inside the component that will update the rating state when called.
successCriteria: The handleRatingClick function is defined with a starNumber parameter and calls setRating(starNumber).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function takes a parameter and calls setRating with that value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. It should take a starNumber parameter and update the rating state using setRating.

steps.title: Define handleMouseLeave function
steps.instruction: Define a function called handleMouseLeave inside your StarRating component that resets the hover state to 0.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setHover(0) to reset the hover value when the mouse leaves the star area.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleMouseLeave function is defined that calls setHover(0) to reset the hover state.
successCriteria: The handleMouseLeave function is defined inside the component and calls setHover(0).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function calls setHover(0) to properly reset the hover state.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named handleMouseLeave that calls setHover(0) to reset the hover state.

steps.title: Return a container div with star buttons
steps.instruction: In your StarRating component, return a div container that contains five button elements inside it. The buttons should be empty for now.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div containing five button elements. Use JSX syntax for the buttons.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div container with five empty button elements inside.
successCriteria: The StarRating component returns a div containing exactly five button elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly five button elements inside the div container.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're returning a div with five button elements inside it.

steps.title: Add star icons and dynamic styling to buttons
steps.instruction: Inside each button element, add a star icon character (★) and apply conditional inline styling to change the button's color based on whether its index is less than or equal to the current hover or rating state.
steps.hint: Use the ternary operator to conditionally set the style property. For example: style={{ color: index <= (hover || rating) ? 'gold' : 'gray' }}
steps.expectedOutcome: Each button will display a star icon and change color dynamically when hovered or clicked.
successCriteria: All five buttons contain a star icon (★) and have conditional inline styling that changes the color based on rating and hover states.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure each button has both the star icon and conditional styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the star character inside each button and applied the conditional styling correctly.

steps.title: Wire event handlers to star buttons
steps.instruction: Add onClick, onMouseEnter, and onMouseLeave event handlers to each button, calling the appropriate handler functions with the star index.
steps.hint: For each button, add onClick={...}, onMouseEnter={...}, and onMouseLeave={...} attributes. Pass the star number (1-5) to the handlers.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring event handlers to buttons
<button onClick={() => handleClick(1)} onMouseEnter={() => handleHover(1)} onMouseLeave={handleLeave}>
  Button 1
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each star button will have click and hover interactivity wired to the state handlers.
successCriteria: All five buttons have onClick, onMouseEnter, and onMouseLeave handlers that call the appropriate functions with the star index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some event handlers, but not all buttons have all three handlers (onClick, onMouseEnter, onMouseLeave) with the correct function calls.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing event handlers. Add onClick, onMouseEnter, and onMouseLeave to each button with the appropriate handler functions.
